title: Thirst Draft: Write Drunk, Edit Never
description:
An event for writers — and for writing. Everyone gets the same prompt when they walk in the door. What ends up on the page is up to you!

Here’s how it works:
Write whatever you want — poem, song, short story, joke… anything works!
Interpret the prompt however you like, but try to incorporate it in some way
Work alone or collaborate with friends/strangers — no word count or time limit
Sign up by 7pm if you want to share your piece on stage, just like an open mic
Want to join, but can’t make it by 6 pm? All good!
Here are some loose times to keep in mind:
Write & Mingle: 6pm to 7pm
Share on Stage: 7pm to 8pm
Drink & Discuss: 8pm to 9pm
No cover, no editing, no AI. Pens and paper will be available, but bring your own if you can. Tip your bartenders and support your fellow writers.
RSVP via Partiful

title: Schwartzy: Release Party
description:
“Light Longs For Us” Release Party
with Visual Projections by Robert Malmberg

Join us for a special evening celebrating the upcoming release of Schwartzy’s new EP, Light Longs For Us.

The night will feature a live performance of the new music accompanied by immersive visual projections from Schwartzy’s longtime creative collaborator Robert Malmberg, creating a singular audiovisual experience designed specifically for the evening.

Following the performance, we’ll keep things moving with a DJ set late into the night—a chance to celebrate the record, spend time with friends old and new, and experience Light Longs For Us in a form that won’t exist anywhere else.

To mark the occasion, two tracks from the new EP will be available on a limited-edition 7” vinyl, exclusively at the event. Take home a piece of the night before the full digital release

title: Compass Family Services 2nd Annual Pumpkin Patch
Madrone x SFPL: Blind Book Art Challenge
description:
🎃📚 Join Madrone Art Bar and the SF Public Library for a fun Halloween-themed art event! 👻🖤 6-8PM
📖 Choose a gift-wrapped mystery, horror, or thriller book and create an original artwork inspired by its first paragraph or page, without knowing anything else about the story. Put your imagination, interpretation, and creative instincts to the test as you connect visual art and literature in an unexpected way over drinks and community. 🎨🍷
🖼️ At the end of the evening, participants will have the opportunity to share their artwork and take their book home. 📚
🎨 All art supplies provided, though you’re welcome to bring your own favorite materials.
🕸️ 21+ / 🍕 Outside food welcome!

title: Spooky Garden Reverie Halloween Light Show
APOCALYPSE SUNDAY
description:
So what exactly is APOCALYPSE SUNDAY? Consider it a sort-of variety show for people with very few options left. Primarily a musical revue, APOCALYPSE SUNDAY features the music of Bay Area horrorbilly faves The Pine Box Boys, singers of songs of murder and misery. The Boys will also appear as their alter-ego band Lester T. Raww’s Graveside Quartet, whose music has been described as “Tin Pan Alley charm, with Addams Family grim.” Rounding out the regular entertainment is “Gentleman” Jimmy Hadley and his songs of debauchery and poor life choices. And since variety is the spice of life, each week will feature another SF/Bay Area band or artist.
5-8PM

title: Thirst Draft: Write Drunk, Edit Never
description:
An event for writers — and for writing. Everyone gets the same prompt when they walk in the door. What ends up on the page is up to you!
Here’s how it works:
Write whatever you want — poem, song, short story, joke… anything works!
Interpret the prompt however you like, but try to incorporate it in some way
Work alone or collaborate with friends/strangers — no word count or time limit
Sign up by 7pm if you want to share your piece on stage, just like an open mic
Want to join, but can’t make it by 6 pm? All good!
Here are some loose times to keep in mind:
Write & Mingle: 6pm to 7pm
Share on Stage: 7pm to 8pm
Drink & Discuss: 8pm to 9pm
No cover, no editing, no AI. Pens and paper will be available, but bring your own if you can. Tip your bartenders and support your fellow writers.
